tekiccha.cp: adj. curable; one who can be pardoned.
tekiccha.p: [Tikiccha+ṇa] (ti) CL=7 [Tikicchā+ṇa.(cikitā-saṃ)] (1) It can be curable, Should cure, One who can be pardoned or curable. See also - Atekicca. (2) (Teacher or Doctor) who is related to cure.

D: Tekiccha，【形】 可医治的，可被宽恕的人。（p148）

P: Tekiccha，（adj．） [der．fr．tikiccha] curable； fig．one who can be helped or pardoned．Only in cpds．a° incurable，unpardonable VvA．322 （of a sick person）； DhA．I，25 （id．）； Miln．322； of Devadatta w．ref．to his rebirth in Niraya Vin．II，202=It．85； M．I，393； & sa° pardonable Miln．192，221，344．（Page 306）
U: TEKICCHA：[a] có thể trị được，người có thể tha thứ được
K:
tekiccha：တေကိစ္ဆ（တိ）
[တိကိစ္ဆ+ဏ။ တိကိစ္ဆာ+ဏ။ （စိကိတာ-သံ）]
（၁） ကုစားခြင်းငှါ တတ်ကောင်းသော၊ ကုစား-အပ်-သင့်-ထိုက်-သော၊ ကုစား၍ရနိုင်သော၊ သူ။ အတေကိစ္ဆ-လည်းကြည့်။ （၂） ကုစားခြင်း-ဆေးကုခြင်း-၌ ယှဉ်သော （ဆေးဆရာ）။
R:

ကုစားနိုင်သည်။

V:
Tekicchakārī：He was the son of the brahmin Subandhu，and was so-called because he was brought safely into the world with the aid of physicians．When Tekicchakārī was grown up his father，by his wisdom and policy，incurred the jealousy and suspicion of Cānakka，minister of Candagutta，who had him thrown into prison．Tekicchakārī，in his fright，fled，and，taking refuge with a forest-dwelling monk，entered the Order and dwelt in the open air，never sleeping and heedless of heat and cold．Māra，in the guise of a cowherd，tried to tempt him，but he developed insight and became an arahant．



In the time of Vipassī Buddha he was born in a physician’s family and cured a monk，named Asoka，and many others．Eight kappas ago he was a king named Sabbosadha （Thag．384-6； ThagA．i．440f）．



He is probably identical with Tikicchaka of the Apadāna （i．190）．
